audit.whatIsWrong: Slicing Maelstrom is described as 'a point-blank AoE stun' (mid) that 'locks you in place' (spikes[1]). Riot's text says it summons a storm that strikes nearby enemy champions for magic damage — 550 range, flat 120s cooldown, no stun of its own. The stun comes from Mark of the Storm stacking to three off the repeated strikes. Lightning Rush is likewise named everywhere with no numbers: 80 energy, 10/9/8/7/6s, move speed on entry and attack speed on exit.
audit.why: The distinction is the whole fight. A player who believes R is an instant stun writes off the six-second window before the third mark lands; a player who knows the stun is stacked knows to E out of the storm's radius after the first tick instead of standing in it waiting to be locked. And the exit attack speed on Lightning Rush is why he wins the trade after he kites — it is not a pure escape.
audit.corrected: spikes[1].text and mid now carry 550 range, the flat 120s, and Mark of the Storm as the stun source. whys[1], dosFull[0].d and report[5].t now carry Lightning Rush's 80 energy, 10s rank-1 cooldown, and the speed-in / attack-speed-out profile.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on the page tells the player Electrical Surge is an on-hit ability.
audit.why: missingInteractions flags onhit-itemization: his W applies on-hit and scales with attack speed, and Lightning Rush hands him attack speed on exit. Reading his damage as pure ability burst makes armour look relevant when magic resist and health are what the trade actually needs.
audit.corrected: wants.foe[0] rewritten to name Electrical Surge as the on-hit, attack-speed-scaling tool that stacks the third mark.

edits.before: Levels 4 through 5 are a genuine test of patience: Kennen pokes you off the wave with Q and his passive mark mechanic, and if you get triple-stunned by the passive proc you take a full combo standing still. Respect that window completely — E absorbs one Q, but the passive stun on three marks is your death sentence if you are not at full HP. At Level 6 his R Slicing Maelstrom changes the math entirely: it is a point-blank AoE stun on a moderate cooldown that counters your all-in directly. The only way to use your own R productively here is to force his R first — bait it with an aggressive Q approach, back off, then re-engage once it is down and Wind Slash as he burns energy running away.
edits.after: Levels 4 through 5 are a genuine test of patience: Kennen pokes you off the wave with Q and his passive mark mechanic, and if you get triple-stunned by the passive proc you take a full combo standing still.
